mainTopic: Laws of the שופר on ראש השנה: forbidden cutting, liquids placed inside it, and whether women and children may blow it
overview: This amud continues the משנה's rules about the שופר on ראש השנה. First the גמרא explains that cutting the שופר is forbidden both with a sickle (a שבות) and with a knife (a לא תעשה). It explains that the extra mention of the Torah prohibition follows the style 'זו ואין צריך לומר זו'. Next it learns that water or wine may be put into the שופר but urine may not, and it identifies this as the view of אבא שאול, who forbids urine out of respect. The משנה says children are not stopped from blowing, which implies women are stopped. A ברייתא says women are not stopped either, and אביי answers that this is a dispute between רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון, as seen in their argument about women doing סמיכה. Finally, רבי אלעזר and a ברייתא say we train children to blow even on שבת. The גמרא then points out a contradiction inside that ברייתא, and its answer begins here and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The משנה forbids cutting the שופר on יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: one may not cut the שופר on ראש השנה, whether the method is forbidden only rabbinically (שבות) or by the Torah (לא תעשה).
steps.simpleTranslation: And we do not cut it, whether with something that is forbidden because of a rabbinic decree or with something that is forbidden because of a Torah prohibition.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a line from the משנה to set up its explanation. The line says you cannot cut the שופר on יום טוב, whether the cutting is a rabbinic violation or a Torah violation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה names two levels of forbidden action: a שבות, which the Rabbis forbade, and a לא תעשה, which the Torah forbids. Even though blowing שופר is a מצוה, it does not override either level. The גמרא will now explain which tool belongs to which level.

keyTerms.meaning: cutting (here, trimming or shaping the שופר)
an action forbidden on שבת or יום טוב by rabbinic decree
a Torah prohibition (a negative commandment)

phrases.english: And we do not cut it (the shofar),
phrases.notes: Quoted from the משנה; it continues the list of things not done for the שופר on יום טוב.

phrases.english: whether with something that is forbidden because of a rabbinic decree

phrases.aramaic: וּבֵין בְּדָבָר שֶׁהוּא מִשּׁוּם לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה.
phrases.english: or with something that is forbidden because of a Torah prohibition.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's list of forbidden actions for the שופר from the previous section of the daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Cutting the שופר on יום טוב is forbidden, whether it is a rabbinic or a Torah violation.

steps.title: Sickle is rabbinic, knife is Torah-level
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the two categories: cutting with a sickle (מגלא) is a שבות, while cutting with a knife (סכינא) is a לא תעשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Because of a rabbinic decree' means a sickle. 'A Torah prohibition' means a knife.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives an example of each category from the משנה. A sickle is the rabbinic case, and a knife is the Torah case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A knife is the normal tool for cutting a horn, so using it is a real מלאכה and is forbidden by the Torah. A sickle is an unusual tool for this job, and doing a מלאכה in an unusual way is only forbidden מדרבנן. So the difference between the two cases is how the cutting is done.

keyTerms.meaning: a sickle (an unusual tool for cutting a horn)
a knife (the normal cutting tool)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the sickle cut is allowed because it is 'only' rabbinic. The משנה forbids both. The difference is only in the level of the prohibition, not in whether you may do it.

phrases.english: 'Because of a rabbinic decree' means a sickle.
phrases.notes: Cutting in an unusual way, so only rabbinically forbidden.

phrases.english: 'A Torah prohibition' means a knife.
phrases.notes: The normal way of cutting, so a full מלאכה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the two categories named in the משנה line quoted in Step 1.

steps.title: Why mention the Torah prohibition at all?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if even a rabbinic violation is forbidden, it is obvious that a Torah violation is forbidden. Why does the משנה need to say it?
steps.simpleTranslation: Now that you said that something forbidden because of a rabbinic decree is not allowed, is it necessary to say that a Torah prohibition is not allowed?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the wording of the משנה. If even the lighter (rabbinic) violation is forbidden, the heavier (Torah) one is obviously forbidden too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה is not supposed to contain extra words. Mentioning the לא תעשה after the שבות seems to add nothing, since it follows automatically. The גמרא wants to know why the extra clause is there.

keyTerms.meaning: 'now' — used to open a 'how much more so' challenge
'is it necessary (to say)?' — it is obvious

phrases.english: Now that you said that something forbidden because of a rabbinic decree is not allowed —
is it necessary to say that a Torah prohibition is not allowed?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the משנה's phrasing that was just quoted and explained.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's inclusion of the לא תעשה clause
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the lighter prohibition is forbidden, the heavier one is obvious, so the second clause seems unnecessary.

steps.title: A teaching style: 'this, and certainly that'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה uses the style 'זו ואין צריך לומר זו', 'this, and no need to say that', which lists the obvious case too.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה teaches in the style of 'this, and it is not necessary to say that.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. The משנה uses a familiar style where it states one case and then adds the obvious case, without trying to teach anything new.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא admits that the לא תעשה clause adds no new law. It explains the clause as a known way the משנה speaks: it says 'not only this, but of course that.' So there is no extra law hidden here; it is a matter of phrasing.

keyTerms.meaning: 'this, and it is unnecessary to say that' — a style that lists an obvious case alongside a new one
'it teaches' (the משנה or ברייתא states)

steps.whatToRemember: Cutting the שופר on יום טוב is forbidden both with a sickle (rabbinic) and with a knife (Torah). The knife case is mentioned in the style of 'זו ואין צריך לומר זו', so it adds no new law.

phrases.aramaic: זוֹ וְאֵין צָרִיךְ לוֹמַר זוֹ קָתָנֵי.
phrases.english: It teaches in the style of 'this, and it is not necessary to say that.'

steps.triggerLanguage: זוֹ וְאֵין צָרִיךְ לוֹמַר זוֹ קָתָנֵי
steps.terutzResolutionType: Stylistic explanation: the extra clause is a known teaching style, not a new law.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The לא תעשה clause looked like a needless repetition.
steps.terutzMaskana: The clause is part of the 'זו ואין צריך לומר זו' style and is not a problem.

steps.title: משנה permits putting water or wine in the shofar
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה: if one wants to put water or wine into the שופר on יום טוב, he may.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if he wants to put water or wine into it, he may put it in.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה, which permits pouring water or wine into the שופר. This sets up the inference in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Liquid inside the שופר helps clean it and make its sound clearer. Pouring liquid in is not a forbidden מלאכה, so the משנה allows it even on יום טוב. The word 'אבל' contrasts this permission with the forbidden actions listed before.

keyTerms.meaning: to put into it
he may put (it in) — a permission

phrases.english: But if he wants to put into it
phrases.notes: Quoted from the משנה; 'but' contrasts with the forbidden actions before it.

phrases.english: water or wine — he may put it in.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל אִם רָצָה לִיתֵּן לְתוֹכוֹ מַיִם אוֹ יַיִן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה: what may be done to improve the שופר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Putting water or wine into the שופר on יום טוב is allowed.

steps.title: Inference: water or wine yes, urine no
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא infers from the משנה's wording that only water or wine is allowed, but urine (מי רגלים) is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Water or wine, yes. Urine, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads closely into the משנה. Because the משנה names only water or wine, it implies that urine is not permitted. This sets up the next question about whose view this is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Urine was known to be good for cleaning a horn, so one might have thought it is also allowed. The משנה's specific list suggests it is excluded. This exclusion needs a source, and the גמרא will find one next.

keyTerms.meaning: urine
'yes' (in a דיוק: this is allowed)

phrases.english: Water or wine — yes,
urine — no.
phrases.notes: Urine actually helps the horn, which is why the exclusion is notable.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַיִם אוֹ יַיִן — אֵין, מֵי רַגְלַיִם — לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an inference (דיוק) from the משנה line just quoted.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Implied from the משנה: urine may not be put into the שופר.

steps.title: Who is the author of the משנה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא holds the view of the משנה that urine is excluded.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which תנא wrote the משנה, since the inference about urine needs a known source. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ban on urine is not obvious, since urine helps the שופר. Asking 'מני' looks for a named תנא whose reasoning explains the ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: our משנה
'who is it?' — asking which תנא the source follows

phrases.english: Our משנה — whose view is it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Looks for the author behind the inference made in Step 6.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא holds that water or wine is permitted but urine is not?

steps.title: It is אבא שאול: urine is forbidden out of respect
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה follows אבא שאול, who says in a ברייתא that water or wine is permitted to clear the sound, but urine is forbidden out of respect.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is אבא שאול, as it was taught in a ברייתא: אבא שאול says, water or wine is permitted, to make it clear. Urine is forbidden, because of respect.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא identifies the משנה as following אבא שאול. It quotes a ברייתא where he allows water or wine but forbids urine because it is disrespectful.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to אבא שאול, urine is not forbidden because of any שבת or יום טוב law. It is forbidden because putting urine into an object used for a מצוה is disrespectful. This explains why the משנה lists only water and wine, even though urine would help the sound.

keyTerms.meaning: a תנא whose view the משנה follows here
'as it was taught' — introduces a ברייתא
to clean or clarify it (to make the sound clear)
because of respect (for the מצוה object)

steps.whatToRemember: Water or wine may be put into the שופר on יום טוב to clear its sound. Urine is forbidden according to אבא שאול, whom our משנה follows, out of respect for the מצוה object, not because of a יום טוב prohibition.
steps.confusionAlert: The ban on urine is not a שבת or יום טוב law. It is about כבוד for the שופר, so it has nothing to do with the cutting prohibitions earlier here.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows a principle that objects used for a מצוה must be treated with respect, even when a disrespectful method would work better.

phrases.english: It is Abba Shaul.
As it was taught in a baraita: Abba Shaul says:

phrases.aramaic: מַיִם אוֹ יַיִן — מוּתָּר, כְּדֵי לְצַחְצְחוֹ.
phrases.english: Water or wine — permitted, in order to make it (its sound) clear.
Urine — forbidden, because of respect.
phrases.notes: The reason is respect for the מצוה object, not a יום טוב law.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּא שָׁאוּל הִיא. דְּתַנְיָא, אַבָּא שָׁאוּל אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 7 by naming the תנא and quoting his ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה follows אבא שאול, who permits water or wine and forbids urine out of respect.

steps.title: The משנה: children are not stopped from blowing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה: we do not stop children from blowing the שופר.
steps.simpleTranslation: We do not stop the children from blowing the שופר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings up a new line from the משנה to discuss. This sets up the next move, where the גמרא will learn something from what the line leaves out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Children are not yet obligated in מצוות, so you might think there is no reason to let them blow on יום טוב. The משנה says we let them, because it trains them for when they grow up.

keyTerms.meaning: We stop / prevent
Young children
To blow (the שופר)

phrases.english: We do not stop the children from blowing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the discussion of putting water or wine into the שופר to the next ruling in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Children are allowed to blow the שופר on ראש השנה; we do not stop them.

steps.title: Inference: women would be stopped
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reasons that since the משנה mentions only children, women must be stopped from blowing.
steps.simpleTranslation: This implies that women are stopped.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא makes a deduction from what the משנה left out. This sets up a challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה went out of its way to say children may blow. If women were also allowed, the משנה could have said so, so the גמרא concludes that women are not allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: This implies (a deduction from the wording)
Women

phrases.english: This implies that women are stopped,
phrases.notes: An inference from what the משנה does not say.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a deduction from the משנה line quoted in step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: By implication, the משנה holds that women who want to blow are stopped.

steps.title: Challenge from a ברייתא: women are not stopped either
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says we stop neither women nor children from blowing on יום טוב, which contradicts the inference from the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it was taught in a ברייתא: We do not stop either the women or the children from blowing on a Festival!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the deduction it just made. A ברייתא openly says that women are also allowed to blow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's wording implies women are stopped, but the ברייתא says they are not stopped. Both cannot be true, so the גמרא needs an explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: But it was taught in a ברייתא (introduces a challenge)
Festival day (here, ראש השנה)

phrases.aramaic: וְהָתַנְיָא: אֵין מְעַכְּבִין לֹא אֶת הַנָּשִׁים
phrases.english: But it was taught: We do not stop the women

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא אֶת הַתִּינוֹקוֹת מִלִּתְקוֹעַ בְּיוֹם טוֹב!
phrases.english: nor the children from blowing on a Festival!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the inference made in step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: The inference that the משנה holds women are stopped from blowing.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא explicitly says women are not stopped, which contradicts the משנה's implication.

steps.title: אביי: two different תנאים
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that the משנה follows רבי יהודה, while the ברייתא follows רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: It is not difficult. This one follows רבי יהודה; that one follows רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי solves the contradiction by saying the two sources reflect two different opinions among the תנאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two sources are not arguing about the facts. They follow different views on whether women may do a מצוה they are not obligated in. רבי יהודה says no, so the משנה stops women. רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון say yes, so the ברייתא allows them.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult (introduces an answer)
אביי, an אמורא

phrases.english: Abaye said: It is not difficult:
This (the Mishnah) follows Rabbi Yehuda,
that (the Baraita) follows Rabbi Yosei and Rabbi Shimon.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning the two sources to different תנאים (מחלוקת)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה and the ברייתא seemed to contradict each other about women.
steps.terutzMaskana: They do not contradict each other. The משנה follows רבי יהודה and the ברייתא follows רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון.

steps.title: Source for the dispute: women and סמיכה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא where רבי יהודה says women do not do סמיכה, while רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון say women may do it if they choose.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: 'Speak to the children of Israel' — the sons of Israel place their hands, but the daughters of Israel do not place their hands; these are the words of רבי יהודה. רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון say: Women placing their hands is optional.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows where this dispute between the תנאים is found, to back up אביי's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: סמיכה is a מצוה that women are not obligated in. רבי יהודה does not let women do it, and the same reasoning would stop them from blowing the שופר. רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון let women do it voluntarily (רשות), and the same reasoning would let them blow.

keyTerms.meaning: Placing hands on a קרבן before it is slaughtered (סמיכה)
Literally 'sons of Israel'
Optional, allowed but not required

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון do not say women are obligated in סמיכה. They only say women may choose to do it.
steps.whyThisMatters: This dispute about whether women may do מצוות they are not obligated in applies across many areas, not only שופר.

phrases.english: As it was taught: 'Speak to the children of Israel.'
phrases.notes: ויקרא א:ב, in the section about סמיכה on a קרבן.

phrases.english: The sons of Israel place hands,
but the daughters of Israel do not place hands,
these are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.
Rabbi Yosei and Rabbi Shimon say:
Women placing hands is optional.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the dispute that אביי relied on in step 12.
steps.raayaObject: אביי's claim that רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי/רבי שמעון disagree about women doing מצוות they are not obligated in.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about סמיכה, based on 'דבר אל בני ישראל'.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה (women are stopped) follows רבי יהודה. The ברייתא (women are not stopped) follows רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון, who allow women to do non-obligatory מצוות voluntarily.

steps.title: The משנה: we work with children until they learn
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה: we actively work with children until they learn to blow.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we occupy ourselves with them until they learn.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to the next line in the משנה. It says we do more than just let children blow; we help train them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Not stopping children is passive. Working with them is active: we teach and encourage them so they learn to blow properly.

keyTerms.meaning: We occupy ourselves with them / work with them
Until they learn

phrases.english: But we occupy ourselves with them until they learn.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה from step 9 with a new clause.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: We actively help children practice blowing until they learn.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: even on שבת
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר says that working with children to teach them to blow is allowed even on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: Even on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר adds to the משנה: the training of children is allowed even when ראש השנה falls on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You might think that on שבת, when blowing is more restricted, we should not train children. רבי אלעזר says the permission still applies.

keyTerms.meaning: רבי אלעזר, an אמורא
Even on שבת

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said: Even on Shabbat.
phrases.notes: Even when ראש השנה falls on שבת and the שופר is not blown for the מצוה (outside the מקדש), we may still train children.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands the משנה line from step 14 to include שבת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Training children to blow the שופר is allowed even on שבת.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רבי אלעזר
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא also says we work with children until they learn, even on שבת, and that we do not stop them from blowing on שבת, and certainly not on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught so: We occupy ourselves with them until they learn, even on שבת. And we do not stop the children from blowing on שבת, and needless to say on a Festival.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says the same thing as רבי אלעזר, to support him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא matches רבי אלעזר's ruling about שבת. It also uses the 'אין צריך לומר' style: if children are not stopped on שבת, they are certainly not stopped on a weekday יום טוב.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also taught this way (introduces support)
Needless to say

phrases.english: It was also taught so:

phrases.aramaic: מִתְעַסְּקִין בָּהֶן עַד שֶׁיִּלְמְדוּ, אֲפִילּוּ בְּשַׁבָּת.
phrases.english: We occupy ourselves with them until they learn, even on Shabbat.
And we do not stop the children from blowing on Shabbat,
and needless to say on a Festival.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי אלעזר's statement in step 15.
steps.raayaObject: רבי אלעזר's ruling that training children is allowed even on שבת.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that says the same thing explicitly.

steps.title: Contradiction inside the ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא seems to contradict itself. 'We work with them' implies we actively tell children to blow, but 'we do not stop them' implies we only allow it without telling them.
steps.simpleTranslation: This itself is difficult! You said: We occupy ourselves with them until they learn, even on שבת — so evidently we tell them from the outset, 'Blow!' And then it teaches: We do not stop them — it is only stopping that we don't do, but from the outset we do not tell them 'Blow!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that two lines in the same ברייתא seem to contradict each other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first line suggests we actively encourage children to blow (לכתחלה). The second line, 'we do not stop them', suggests we only allow it passively and do not tell them to blow. The same ברייתא cannot say both.

keyTerms.meaning: This itself is difficult (an internal contradiction)
Evidently / this shows
From the outset, as the preferred approach
Blow! (a command)

steps.confusionAlert: There are two levels here. 'Not stopping' means we only allow it. 'Telling them to blow' means we actively encourage it. The contradiction is about which of these the ברייתא means.

phrases.english: This itself is difficult,
you said: We occupy ourselves with them until they learn,
and even on Shabbat —
evidently, from the outset we say: Blow!
And then it teaches: We do not stop them —
it is only stopping that we do not do,
but from the outset we do not say: Blow!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ברייתא brought as support in step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's two clauses: 'מתעסקין בהן' and 'אין מעכבין'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'מתעסקין' implies we actively tell children to blow from the outset, while 'אין מעכבין' implies we only refrain from stopping them. The two clauses contradict each other.

steps.title: Opening the answer: the two phrases are about different cases
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins resolving the contradiction in the ברייתא by saying it is not really a problem, and it starts to explain that one phrase applies 'here,' in one case.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is starting its answer to the contradiction from step 17. This line is a setup that opens a 'here… here…' answer, which finishes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase לא קשיא tells us the גמרא thinks the two phrases in the ברייתא do not truly clash. The word כאן ('here') signals that the גמרא will apply 'we work with them' to one kind of child and 'we do not stop them' to a different kind of child. The exact cases are spelled out on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It is not difficult.' The standard opening for an answer that removes a contradiction.
'Here.' Used to point to one specific case. It usually comes in a pair (כָּאן… כָּאן…) to split two rulings between two situations.
A difficulty or contradiction. Here it refers to the clash inside the ברייתא from step 17.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the answer is finished here. The word כאן only opens the split. The actual cases being contrasted come at the start of the next amud.

phrases.english: This is not difficult:
phrases.notes: Signals that the contradiction from step 17 is about to be resolved.

phrases.english: Here,
phrases.notes: Opens the first half of a 'here… here…' split. Each phrase of the ברייתא will be assigned to a different case.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the קשיא of step 17 by beginning to divide the two phrases of the ברייתא between two different cases.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Case distinction (כאן… כאן…): each clause of the ברייתא refers to a different situation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We assumed 'we work with them' and 'we do not stop them' describe the same children, so the two phrases seem to contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: The phrases describe different cases, so there is no contradiction. The exact distinction is completed on the next amud.
